description: Coverage accounting. 'quarantine' lists tests that no CI leg executes, each with an owner, a review date and the gap it leaves; the Safety evidence job fails on any other never-executed test. 'dispositions' explain removed or weakened coverage; check_coverage_regression.py accepts only dispositions added by the same change. See docs/rules/safety-evidence.md.

quarantine.reason: Collation.Default snapshots the culture once per process, so the test passes only as the first LiteDB use in the process; after another test created a database it sees that culture instead of 'fi'.
quarantine.gap: A new database taking its collation from the current thread culture is not asserted on any CI leg; product behaviour (process-wide snapshot) decides whether the test can be made order-independent.

quarantine.reason: Not supported yet: rebuilding 'ana'/'ANA' from en-US/None to en-US/IgnoreCase throws 'Cannot insert duplicate key' instead of recording the collision in _rebuild_errors.
quarantine.gap: Rebuilding to a collation under which unique keys collide is not exercised; the expected _rebuild_errors behaviour is not implemented.

quarantine.reason: Takes ~102 s (100 iterations with a 1 s sleep; passed 5/5 locally on net10.0). The DiskWriterQueue race of #2127 no longer exists; the queue was removed in 198f0a672.
quarantine.gap: Back-to-back file-backed inserts into 100 recreated databases do not run in CI; the original race cannot recur, so the test is a candidate to retire as obsolete.

dispositions.invariant: Every test leg's results are uploaded and judged; no existing timeout, filter or partition changes.
dispositions.reason: Adds the Safety policy and Safety evidence jobs (10-minute limits) and a results upload for the .NET Framework leg, which uploaded nothing before; existing test steps keep their timeouts and filters.

dispositions.invariant: A checkpoint on a log that answers "cannot sync" never loses a commit and never tears the data file; it retries the log sync and drains the WAL once the log syncs.
dispositions.reason: Decision D and implementation note 12: no in-place overwrite behind a recovery copy that is only in the OS cache, in both commit modes. Without durable commits such a checkpoint now writes nothing and keeps the WAL (it used to overwrite data in write order); with durable commits the commit whose log answers "cannot sync" fails instead (decision 3), so the degraded commit that CheckpointRetriesDurableSyncAfterCommitFallback set up no longer exists. The new tests assert byte-identical files, kept frames, the drain once the log syncs and power-loss images.

dispositions.invariant: Storage that cannot sync never reuses retired WAL slots, and a snapshot checkpoint there keeps the reader's snapshot and every commit.
dispositions.reason: Decision 3 splits the scenario by mode: without durable commits it still appends instead of reusing slots (a checkpoint whose log cannot sync retires nothing, so the slot-clear case is forced by a log that stops syncing at the clears); with durable commits that checkpoint now fails loudly and the engine continues read-only.

dispositions.invariant: A shared connection on a log that cannot sync reports it after later operations reopen engines, never acknowledges a commit as durable there, keeps the reader's snapshot, and a checkpoint whose log cannot sync writes nothing to the data file; a connection that learned its log cannot sync never reuses slots retired there, one that never learned it reuses only slots a durable witness root names, and every power-loss image recovers exactly (implementation note 15).
dispositions.reason: Decisions 3 and D and the retirement proof: with durable commits a commit whose log answers "cannot sync" fails (outcome unknown once its frames reached the OS) and a checkpoint on it fails loudly; without durable commits "cannot sync" is no failure (default A) and the degraded commit is acknowledged, as before. A checkpoint on a log known not to sync, or that stops syncing after its proof, retires and writes nothing; only a log that stops at the sync of the clears leaves cleared slots, which no later engine of this connection reuses. Asserted per mode and stop point, with a second connection. Implementation note 15 drops the log sync an engine made before its first slot reuse: a second connection that never learned the log cannot sync now reuses the witnessed slots (was: one refused sync, then append), checked with power-loss images.

dispositions.invariant: A fresh engine reuses a retired WAL slot only while a root on the device names it, and every power-loss image of the reusing commit recovers exactly the committed rows.
dispositions.reason: Implementation note 15: reusing a retired slot needs no sync of its own (it proved nothing the durable witness root does not, and cost a log sync per shared operation). The test now expects a fresh engine without durable commits to reuse the witnessed slots without syncing first, and adds power-loss images of the log as last synced and with the reused frames written back without their confirmations. The shared-mode test (named at the S09 baseline) is renamed because a second connection that never learned the log cannot sync now reuses the witnessed slots; see 3027-shared-log-cannot-sync.

dispositions.invariant: A database on a log that never syncs stays readable with every committed row, and no format change tears its header.
dispositions.reason: Implementation note 12 and decisions 2, 3 and D: an index migration, a 5.x conversion or a compact promotion overwrites the header behind a journal the log cannot make durable, so it is refused before it writes: the open falls back to read-only, and a compact write stores BSON instead. With durable commits the commit fails before it writes. They used to publish the new format behind an OS-cached journal.

dispositions.invariant: Log storage that rejects sync never corrupts data, a commit is never acknowledged as durable when it is not, and an opted-out checkpoint makes the log durable before it overwrites data.
dispositions.reason: Decisions 3 and D: with durable commits a log that cannot sync fails the commit (before it writes, or with outcome unknown when it stops syncing after the frames reached the OS) instead of degrading silently; without durable commits it degrades and a checkpoint writes nothing behind it. The opted-out checkpoint's sync order gained the data sync first (a checkpoint writes only to a data file that just synced), so that test was renamed with the new order.

dispositions.invariant: Recovery from an OS-cached promotion journal never replaces a valid header with the journal's copy.
dispositions.reason: e4b9553fd: before the sync that retires a header journal, recovery writes the header back as read (a failed sync's pages may be marked clean, fsyncgate). The recovered-open check was "no data write at all"; it is now "the data file's bytes are unchanged", which still fails if the journal's copy replaced a valid header.

dispositions.invariant: Each test still asserts the exact position, length and content of the frames it writes; only the layout moved.
dispositions.reason: Decision 11: every non-volatile checksummed WAL generation starts with a header frame (frame 0, a copy of the data header). Expected WAL positions and lengths move by one frame (Disk_Tests, FrameFailure_Tests, LazyChecksumCutover_Tests, WalSlotReuse_Tests); WalPowerLoss_Tests pads one commit when the shifted acknowledged end would fall on a sector boundary, so the torn-sector case it asserts still arises; FailedSafepointWrite_Tests' FailingLog skips the header frame so it still fails the transaction's own frame. No assertion is removed or loosened.

dispositions.invariant: Durable commits on storage that cannot sync, and the opted-out checkpoint's barriers.
dispositions.reason: The two tolerance tests of this file (see 3027-durable-commits-log-cannot-sync) moved to the per-mode tests of CheckpointDurability_Tests, NativeFileSync_Tests and OverwriteBarrier_Tests; one assertion call fewer remains here.

dispositions.invariant: A WAL directory that cannot sync is reported and never loses a commit acknowledged as durable.
dispositions.reason: Decision 9: with durable commits such a directory fails the commit before it writes; without durable commits it keeps committing and reports the log as not durable.

dispositions.invariant: A WAL directory that cannot sync degrades visibly and never loses an acknowledged commit.
dispositions.reason: The evidence test was split by mode (decision 9, see 3027-wal-directory-cannot-sync); the registry names both new tests.

dispositions.invariant: The pinned checksum-wal seed replays the same generated input and I/O trace, and its oracle passes.
dispositions.reason: Every WAL generation now starts with a header frame (decision 11), one more frame write in the trace. Replayed at the S08 head and at each S09 layer (S09a 4ee70dd56, S09b 706aeef58, S09c e65387a91) on .NET 10: the trace changed only at the header-frame layer (S09b), and with WriteHeaderFrame disabled there the old hash returns. The input hash is unchanged, the oracle passes, the new hash matches on .NET 8 and .NET 10 (and #3027's final pin), and the old one stays under previousHashes.

dispositions.invariant: The pinned crash seeds replay the same generated input and I/O trace, and their crash-recovery oracle passes.
dispositions.reason: The durability protocol changes which syncs and writes a checkpoint, a commit and recovery perform. Replayed at the S08 head (unchanged, so nothing is owed to S08) and at each S09 layer on .NET 10: every seed changed at the durability-accounting layer (S09a: data syncs before a checkpoint writes, header write-back before a journal is retired, overwrite barriers; disabling the checkpoint's data sync or the write-back alone changes but does not restore the S08 hashes, so the S09a change is their combination), at the header-frame layer (S09b; with WriteHeaderFrame disabled the S09a hashes return) and at the admission layer (S09c; without RequireDurableCommit's once-per-log proof of the log file and its directory the S09b hashes return, while skipping only the data barrier changes nothing). Each oracle passes, the final hashes match on .NET 8 and .NET 10 and equal #3027's final pins, and the S08-era and per-layer hashes stay under previousHashes.

dispositions.invariant: Every .NET Framework test runs to completion and reports on each CI run.
dispositions.reason: The net481 job ran 14m32s at the S08 head (PR #3061) and 19m33s at #3027's head, which had been cancelled at the 20-minute limit after 4713 tests ran without a failure. The difference is the durability suites this layer adds (power-loss models, header frames, retirement and read-only continuation tests), which leaves no margin under 20 minutes. 30 minutes lets the whole leg finish; the .NET jobs allow 40. No filter, partition or test changed.
